Passed ENW401 or (ENS412 & ENS422) or ENT503
K15 onward: Passed EAL201 & SSC302c & LTG202
info.description: This introductory course provides an instructional manual to equip students with a theoretical basis for, and essential skills in, Interpretation. Two common types are put into focus; Consecutive Interpreting and Simultaneous Interpreting. The objective is to train students to be capable of interpreting in various fields and settings.
info.studentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

- Actively participate in class activities

- Fulfill tasks given by the teacher after class

- Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes

- Read the textbook in advance

materials.author: Aline Ferreira (Editor) & John W. Schwieter (Editor)

clos.loDetails: Explain the correlation between a good public speaker and an interpreter.
Organize, select and develop interpreting skills in various fields and settings.
Recognize the preparation stage and the attitute to overcome several problems that may occur during the actual interpreting setting.
Use several strategies to help cope with the combined difficulty of complexity and speed.
Identify units of meaning in the speech and recognize the importance of two kinds of clusters.
Use general adverbial clauses in various proper ways.
Translate the importance of identifying figures of speech and technical measurement to convey the meaning.
Use several strategies to cope with quotations, allusions, and transposition.
Understand the value of teamwork skills and attitudes in interpretation.

+ Interpreter's roles
+ Technology & Interpreting
- Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities of an interpreter
+ Codes of Ethics and Standards of Practice
+Professional Credentials and Qualifications

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to interpreting in a business setting.
assessments.note: Teacher is asked to write a field trip proposal with specific details and send it to the person in charge.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 1-3) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈200words, comprised of two parts, one in English [100 words], one in Vietnamese [100 words]), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 4-6) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈200words, comprised of two parts, one in English [100 words], one in Vietnamese [100 words]), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test the student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 7-9) to simultaneous interpreting.
assessments.note: The teacher shall prepare 5-6 audio files (≈2minutes/file) relating to several specific topics, of which the students will be informed in advance. On the test day, students will be divided into groups of 4 or 5. All members will be standing at different positions in class, simultaneously listening to the same audio and recording their interpretation using a smartphone. Upon completion, students are asked to send the record to the teacher immediately.

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to consecutive interpreting (both ENG-VIE and VIE-ENG processes). Topics: 1. Education 2. Entertainment 3. Technology 4. Environment/Nature 5. Business, Economics and Finance 6. Tourism 7. Family and Friends 8. Health 9. Culture 10. Arts
assessments.note:
The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈360-400 words, comprised of two parts, one in English [180-200 words], one in Vietnamese [180-200 words]), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance.

Students take the exam individually. Students will randomly pick 2 texts, then listen to the audios or to the examiners to read the texts and interpret.

Students are allowed to take notes in the exam room.
